card.name: Words mid-clause in old historical prose
card.fires_on: Ordinary connecting or verb words in the middle of a clause in older, literary or historical encyclopedia-style prose, such as 'with', 'of', 'are' or 'devoted'. It comes just before the sentence's key noun or adjective.

modes.label: 'with' in descriptions
modes.description: The word 'with' after a verb or participle in historical or geographic description.
modes.example: Its boundaries cannot be defined<< with>> certainty.

modes.label: Verbs in biographical sentences
modes.description: A verb such as 'devoted' or 'spend' in a biographical account of a famous person's childhood.
modes.example: he<< devoted>> all his energy and knowledge to their education

modes.label: Words before a descriptive modifier
modes.description: An adjective or link word placed right before a noun in formal prose.

card.plain: It fires on small in-sentence words in old-fashioned historical writing, not on any medical content.
